text: So, is Carrick failing? Five league games cannot erase what he achieved across seventeen last season. United also returned to the Champions League with a four-nil win over Sabah. The honest verdict is harder: Carrick solved the first problem, clarity, and has now met the second, repeatability. His team can punish space. It has not proved it can create against caution, defend after its own attacks, or sustain collective intensity when momentum turns. Sacking him would not answer those questions. Protecting him from them would be just as dangerous. Manchester United do not need another saviour with a new diagram. They need Carrick and the hierarchy to make one football idea survive bad form, different opponents, and the next transfer window. Until that happens, every rebuild will keep looking like progress right before the next reset. The next phase therefore needs a different kind of patience. It is not patience with poor performances for their own sake; it is patience with a clearly defined model while demanding evidence that the model is becoming more resilient. United should be able to explain what they want the full-backs, pivots, wingers and first defender to do in every game state. If they can, Carrick has a platform. If they cannot, the next reset will only rename the same problem.
